t: Classical Chinese, the written language of Confucius, the philosophers and the historians of ancient China, remained the standard written language of China for more than two thousand years, long after the spoken language had changed beyond recognition.

Written in characters that record meaning as well as sound, it was read across East Asia: Korea, Japan and Vietnam used it for government, scholarship and literature, each reading it with its own pronunciation.
Replaced by the vernacular in the 20th century, it remains the foundation of Chinese literature and idiom and is still studied in schools throughout East Asia.
dyk: Because Chinese characters convey meaning whatever their pronunciation, scholars from China, Korea, Japan and Vietnam who could not speak each other’s languages could converse by writing Classical Chinese on paper, a practice known as “brush talk”.
ev: Diviners of the Shang kings carve the earliest known Chinese writing on oracle bones at Anyang
The Analects, the Mencius and the Zhuangzi set the model of the classical written language
The First Emperor of Qin standardises the Chinese script across his empire
Xu Shen completes the Shuowen Jiezi, the first dictionary to analyse the structure of characters
The Diamond Sutra in Chinese, the earliest dated printed book, is made in China
King Sejong of Korea promulgates the Hangul alphabet as an alternative to Chinese characters
The Kangxi Dictionary is completed, listing more than 47,000 characters
China’s Ministry of Education orders primary schools to teach the vernacular instead of Classical Chinese

f.family: Sino-Tibetan: the Sinitic branch, ancestor of the modern Chinese languages
f.script: Chinese characters, from the oracle-bone script of the Shang to the standard forms of the Qin and Han
f.earliest: Oracle-bone inscriptions of the Shang dynasty, about 1250 BCE; the classics of the Zhou period, from the 6th to the 3rd centuries BCE
f.status: Replaced as the standard written language by vernacular Chinese after 1919; still taught in schools across the Chinese-speaking world and in Japan and Korea
